gaps.lead: As soon as the results were announced, people started celebrating.
gaps.sentence: The results had ___ people started celebrating.
gaps.explanation: No sooner had the results been announced than… — reordered to fit the frame.

gaps.lead: The old bridge is still used by locals.
gaps.explanation: Passive is used by locals → active: locals still use.

gaps.lead: Their wedding will take place in June.
gaps.explanation: Weddings/concerts are held: will be held (in June).

gaps.lead: My advice is to check the contract carefully.
gaps.explanation: had better + infinitive (without to): had better check.

gaps.lead: Her French improved because she lived in Lyon.
gaps.sentence: Her French improved as ___ in Lyon.
gaps.explanation: as a result of + noun/-ing: as a result of living.

gaps.lead: I'm afraid this is the last tin of paint we have.
gaps.hint: run out of = have none left
gaps.explanation: run out of = have no more of something left.
